newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps steady, Brent CFDs gain slightly.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps steady, Brent CFDs gain slightly.

text.p: European oil swaps were broadly steady on Tuesday showing only minor variation from Monday's levels, with the exception of Brent CFDs which were 10 cents or so stronger.
Dealers said attention was focused on the APIs, due out later today.
Gasoline lost some of its sparkle, but its place as a leader of the energy complex was barely dented with swaps losing 50 cents or so.
Brent crude CFDs were quiet amid firmer values while naphtha lost ground further out but managed to edge a touch higher on August.
Heavy fuel was steady and the high/low spread narrowed with easier low sulphur fuel swaps.
Gasoline activity was focused on August and spread trade. Dealers said $199.00, $199.50, $199.75, $200.00 and then $199.00 were done for August in that chronological order.
September was pegged around $191.75-192.00 ensuring the August/September spread held steady at around $7.00 a tonne.
Tight physical prompt supplies kept prices firm, but fresh material from August 15 onwards accounted for the sharp backwardation, traders said.
Brent CFDs gained a few cents, but only one deal, an August 4-8 done at September Brent flat, was concluded.
CFDs for the balance of this week were pegged around +12 cents from +8 cents against September with August 4-8 put at flat from - 4 cents.
August 11-15 gained to -5 cents from -12 cents while August 18-22 firmed to -8 cents from -22 cents.
Heavy fuel swaps for August remained around $89-90, and $90 traded. September was valued at $90 with 4Q seen at $94.75 and 1Q at $97.75, but nothing was heard traded.
Low sulphur swaps eased by $1 or so in a very quiet market. August was valued at $93.50. with September about $1 contangoed.
Naphtha swaps were 50 cents firmer on August at $190.50, but the backwardation into September extended to $1.50 or so. Business was sparse with the physical market similarily static.
"There is some trader buying interest, but very little from end-users," said one dealer.
